Career lesson: Safe bench setup, prediction, and measurement
CETa foundation: Voltage, current, resistance, power, polarity, reference, open/short circuit, and Week 1 safety boundaries.
Career prerequisites: Use only the Week 1 CETa electrical-quantity and safety foundation. No prior bench-equipment experience is assumed.
New Career learning: Bench power supply, DMM modes/jacks, current limiting, pre-power inspection, first-power sequence, stop conditions, and hazard logging.
Genuine overlap: CETa explains the electrical quantities; Career turns them into a controlled first-power and measurement workflow.
Future preparation: Creates the bench habits required for every later measurement, bring-up, troubleshooting, and lab task.
Source basis: Georgia Piedmont Technical College — Electronics Technology — current catalog; Portland Community College — EET 101A — Electronic Lab and Essential Work Skills; Fluke — Digital Multimeter Basics; Fluke — Electrical Measurement Safety; NASA — NASA-HDBK-8739.21 — ESD Control

Career lesson: Use expected node values to troubleshoot instead of guessing
CETa foundation: Series/parallel networks, KVL/KCL, dividers, expected node values, and reference-node reasoning.
Career prerequisites: Bring forward Week 1 safe measurement habits plus the Week 2 CETa network equations and expected-node reasoning.
New Career learning: Expected-versus-actual troubleshooting, node tables, first hypotheses, divide-and-conquer test-point selection, and one-change-at-a-time discipline.
Genuine overlap: Career uses the exact CETa node-voltage/current predictions as the known-good baseline for troubleshooting.
Future preparation: Prepares the learner to choose instruments and high-information measurements rather than probe randomly.
Source basis: Georgia Piedmont Technical College — Electronics Technology — current catalog; Portland Community College — EET 101B — Electronic Equipment and Lab Skills; O*NET OnLine / U.S. Department of Labor — Electrical and Electronic Engineering Technologists and Technicians

Career lesson: Measurement planning, probe discipline, and uncertainty
CETa foundation: DMM/scope connection rules, waveform quantities, measurement units, and safe references.
Career prerequisites: Use Week 1 bench safety and the CETa measurement concepts already taught. No professional measurement-planning experience is assumed.
New Career learning: Question-first instrument selection, DMM/bench-supply/scope onboarding, probe/reference discipline, loading/accuracy/resolution, reproducible evidence, and logic-analyzer boundaries.
Genuine overlap: CETa supplies what electrical quantities and waveforms mean; Career teaches how a technician chooses and configures the instrument that can answer a specific question.
Future preparation: Becomes the common measurement workflow for filters, semiconductors, digital buses, MCU bring-up, RF work, and automated test.
Source basis: Portland Community College — EET 101A — Electronic Lab and Essential Work Skills; Portland Community College — EET 101B — Electronic Equipment and Lab Skills; Fluke — Digital Multimeter Basics; Tektronix — The XYZs of Oscilloscopes; O*NET OnLine / U.S. Department of Labor — Electrical and Electronic Engineering Technologists and Technicians

Career lesson: Turn time-domain measurements into filter and fault evidence
CETa foundation: Capacitance, RC time behavior, frequency response, and filter fundamentals.
Career prerequisites: Use the Week 3 measurement workflow plus CETa RC/filter behavior. The learner should already know amplitude, period, frequency, and time constant.
New Career learning: Turn time-domain observations into evidence about cutoff, charging/discharging, distortion, and fault location.
Genuine overlap: Career measures the same RC/filter behavior CETa explains mathematically and physically.
Future preparation: Builds the habit of predicting waveform shape before using a scope for diagnosis.
Source basis: Georgia Piedmont Technical College — Electronics Technology — current catalog; Portland Community College — EET 101B — Electronic Equipment and Lab Skills; Tektronix — The XYZs of Oscilloscopes

Career lesson: A complete troubleshooting loop under a practical gate

Career prerequisites: Use Weeks 1–4 safety, expected-value, and instrument-selection habits. No new tool should appear without explanation.
New Career learning: A complete reproduce → predict → measure → isolate → repair → verify troubleshooting loop under a practical gate.
Genuine overlap: CETa supplies component/circuit behavior; Career organizes that knowledge into a repeatable diagnostic process.
Future preparation: Establishes the troubleshooting model reused through the rest of the course.

Career lesson: Characterize a filter or resonant network like a technician

Career lesson: Troubleshoot with competing hypotheses and high-information tests

Career prerequisites: Use the established troubleshooting loop, schematic/datasheet literacy, and Git/lab-record baseline.

Career lesson: Write and debug small C programs methodically
